Thick Cocoa and Masa Champurrado

Served at: La Noche de Rabanos

Serves 4-6Prep 10 minCook 20 min

Champurrado is a beloved, thick, and comforting Mexican hot chocolate, traditionally made with masa (corn dough) to give it a unique body and subtle corn flavor. It's a perfect warming beverage to enjoy during the cool December evening of La Noche de Rabanos in Oaxaca, Mexico, as you stroll through the main plaza admiring the intricate radish carvings and festive atmosphere.

Ingredients

  • 4 cups (960 ml) water or whole milk, or a combination
  • 1/2 cup (60 g) masa harina
  • 1 (3.2-ounce / 90 g) tablet Mexican chocolate, chopped (such as Ibarra or Abuelita)
  • 1/2 cup (100 g) piloncillo, grated or chopped, or dark brown sugar
  • 1 cinnamon stick (about 3 inches / 7.5 cm)
  • Pinch of salt (optional)

Method

  1. In a small bowl, whisk together the masa harina with 1 cup (240 ml) of the water or milk until smooth and no lumps remain. Set aside.
  2. In a medium saucepan, combine the remaining 3 cups (720 ml) of water or milk, chopped Mexican chocolate, piloncillo (or brown sugar), and cinnamon stick.
  3. Heat the mixture over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until the chocolate and piloncillo are completely melted and dissolved. Do not boil.
  4. Remove the cinnamon stick from the saucepan.
  5. Gradually whisk the masa harina mixture into the chocolate mixture in the saucepan.
  6. Continue to cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly with a whisk or molinillo (Mexican chocolate whisk), for 10 to 15 minutes, or until the champurrado thickens to your desired consistency. Be careful not to let it scorch at the bottom.
  7. Remove from heat and serve hot in mugs.

Tips

  • For an extra frothy champurrado, vigorously whisk it just before serving, or use a molinillo.
  • Adjust the sweetness to your liking by adding more piloncillo or brown sugar.
  • If the champurrado becomes too thick, thin it with a little hot water or milk until it reaches your preferred consistency.
